title: Influence Officer (I) (LtCol to 2ndLt) PMOS, DC I
raw_text:
5.     MOS 1707, Influence Officer (I) (LtCol to 2ndLt) PMOS, DC I

    a. Summary. Influence Officers formulate plans and policies and
coordinate and supervise activities pertaining to Influence Operations
including military information support operations (MISO), civil affairs
operations (CAO) and the integration of Civil Military Operations and provide
the Commander a means to integrate operations in the operational and
information environment to achieve desired outcomes. Influence Officers are
trained personnel who can integrate operations in the information environment
and primarily focus on the planning and execution of MISO, civil authorities’
information support (CAIS) and CAO. MISO are planned operations to convey
selected information and indicators to foreign audiences to influence their
emotions, motives, objective reasoning, and, ultimately, the behavior of
foreign governments, organizations, groups, and individuals in a manner
favorable to the originator’s objectives. CAO are defined as those military
operations planned, supported, executed, or transitioned by CA forces
through, with, or by the OGAs, IPI, IGOs, or NGOs to modify behaviors, to
mitigate or defeat threats to civil society, and to assist in establishing
the capacity for deterring or defeating future civil threats in support of
CMO, facilitation of military operations, or otherwise achieve U.S.
objectives. Influence Officers will serve on staffs at all levels and advise
the commander and staff on the information warfighting function. Influence
Officers integrate capabilities to support the Combatant Command’s Influence
Campaign objectives by supporting the Fleet Marine Force (FMF) missions, as
they enable commanders to shape the information and security environment in
their areas of responsibility (AOR).

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must be a U.S. citizen.

            (2) Must be worldwide deployable.

        (3) Security requirement: must meet sensitive compartmented
information (SCI) eligibility guidelines based on a single scope background
investigation/TS investigation.




                                           1-86                       Enclosure (1)
 1114                                                              NAVMC 1200.1L



       c.   Requirements

        (1) Complete the Psychological Operations Course (A05M301), John F.
Kennedy Special Warfare Center and School, Ft Liberty, NC.

        (2) Complete the Civil Affairs Officer Course (M020A3D), Marine Corps
Civil-Military Operations School (MCCMOS), Quantico, VA.

        (3) Complete the MAGTF operations in the Information Environment
Practitioner Course (MOPC) (M02F2GD), Quantico, VA.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to NAVMC
3500.124A, Information Maneuver Training and Readiness Manual.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Military Officer Special and Tactical Operations Leaders/Managers, All Other
55-1019.

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) Psychological Operations (PSYOP) Officer, 0520.

            (2) Civil-Military Operations Planner, 1708.

            (3) Information Cell Coordinator, 1709.

            (4) Civil Affairs Officer, 1730.

            (5) Basic Information Planner, 1781.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
